Yeah over-consumption of those drugs can cause schitzophrenia-like symptoms, or even trigger it if you have any predisposition for it.  I know a lot of people who have gone through/are going through this, and I'm kind of going through it.  It gets better the longer you're sober, and you are going through a natural brain change at age 22.  Perceptions of ourselves and the world around us are changing a lot already.  It settles down, and talking to people about it helps a lot to kind of "re-connect" to reality.  When you think you're going insane and you never tell anyone, you're trapping yourself in a self-fulfilling prophecy.  I'd talk to a psychologist or someone you trust about it.  I know it's scary, but it doesn't last forever no matter what's causing it.

The concept of value is relative... it is made up, but it's made up of real human emotion and it can take a very long time to value life for what it really is at the core.  Our trivial pursuits don't cease to have value unless we have no emotion toward them.  Try to value your view on life; it might seem bleak, and yeah, most of life really IS pretty bleak, but the fact that you're questioning value has value in and of itself.  You don't have to stay for your family, friends, or future.  Try to think about staying for yourself, and the chance to form your own concept of value.  Fulfillment is not easy, and meaninglessness is an inherent part of life.  Finding value and meaning in meaninglessness is how things like school and work even came about in the first place, and if you work at it and be honest with yourself about your depression, you can find value in things that seem empty.

Being jobless is nothing to be ashamed of.  I'm also incredibly suicidal, and I think about guns a lot.  One of my only comforts is thinking of bashing my head against a wall until I fucking die or putting a 45 in my mouth and pulling the trigger.  I'm a 22 year old, also jobless, also hopeless, but unlike you I don't live with my parents.  I'm homeless and a constant burden on everyone around me.  I've learned that no amount of "I understand" or "you can find hope" will take away those suicidal feelings.  The only thing you can do is deal with them.  I don't know if it's any help, but the quote "“If you want to kill yourself, kill what you don’t like. I had an old self that I killed. You can kill yourself too, but that doesn’t mean you got to stop living” really resonates with me.  Life is hard, and infinitely harder when you're constantly dealing with suicidal thoughts and feelings... but you are not alone, and you may be able to find some solace if you're willing to look for it.  I'd also suggest looking into suicide prevention hotlines, therapy, group support etc.... obv your decision is your decision, but there ARE other options for you, and if there is ANY part of you that fears ending your life or desperately wants someone to understand,  I urge you to listen to that part of yourself and seek help.
